title: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Arrays Similar
summary: Given two arrays of positive integers, nums and target, of equal length, you can perform operations to make nums similar to target.
statement: Given two arrays of positive integers, nums and target, of equal length, you can perform operations to make nums similar to target. An operation consists of adding 2 to one element and subtracting 2 from another. The goal is to find the minimum number of such operations needed. The arrays are considered similar if they have the same frequency of each element.
constraints: nums and target have equal length and positive values; a solution is guaranteed.
One operation adds two to one nums element and subtracts two from another.
Reordering is allowed for the final multiset; return the minimum operations.
hints: Adding or subtracting two preserves parity.
Sort odd and even values together by parity, then by magnitude, in both arrays.
Sum absolute matched differences and divide by four.
Each operation contributes two units on a donor and two on a receiver, so the total absolute distance drops by four.
editorial: Each operation contributes two units on a donor and two on a receiver, so the total absolute distance drops by four.

tests.explanation: Match values by parity; the total transferable distance needs two operations.
After parity-aware matching, one transfer of two makes the multisets equal.
